title: Master HTTP API
what: The master's routes on its loopback: health, one event stream, the cluster, placements run one at a time, and the unit descriptions services hand in, as docs/api.md states them.

title: Command line
what: The bmo-arbiter command line: with no verb it stands as the master, and its verbs install the node arbiter, push rules, ask a placement and open the MCP server, as docs/api.md states them.

title: Placement world
what: The live world a placement acts on: the declarations read from their roots, the node service, each node's shell, the node arbiter's install, and each service's adapter run as its declared command.

title: Node arbiter install
what: Standing and updating the node arbiter on a node: its folder and settings, the files carried from card/, the dump store, the node setup and the user unit, with lend and uninstall beside it.

title: Cluster picture
what: The picture of every card the master keeps from what each slave answers: its units and their places, host memory, turn, queue, claim and stage, and what changed between two readings.

title: Placing services
what: Which service stands on which node, kept by the master: the declarations it reads, the roles and occupants it derives, each adapter it runs, and a request journaled step by step and undone where it fails.

title: Card planner
what: The planner that reads the rules and the picture the slaves gave and decides where an asked unit goes, what is unloaded to make room, whether it comes back, or why the request waits.

title: Node reach
what: How the master reaches a node by its registered name: the node service's target asked through its published client, an ssh batch login or a hub console, and a command run in bash.

title: Master rounds
what: The master's reading rounds: every two seconds it reads each chosen node's arbiter through the node's shell, plans the tickets it finds, and tells the slaves which units to unload and load back.

title: Placement rules
what: The placement rules file: its claimants, node groups, units and eviction rules, each value checked as it is read, and the YAML reader that keeps a mapping in the order a person wrote it.

title: Rules verbs
what: The rules checked, pushed to the nodes they choose, or printed for one node: what a person or an install runs apart from the standing master, with the code root and the push log.
